clue.text: Is this treatment not going to work?

definitions.text: Is this treatment not going to work?

parts.words: Is this treatment not going to work?
parts.note: read as medical treatment that consists of staying off work and lying still, rather than a remedy that fails

explanation.surface: A doubtful patient wonders whether the prescribed therapy will be any use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not going to work' looks like failure, but here it means staying home from the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime of bed and quiet, once prescribed for nervous exhaustion, is exactly a treatment of not going to one's job.

clue.text: Turn to narrow part, making a sort of sweater

parts.note: to turn over is to roll
a neck is a narrow part, as of a bottle

explanation.surface: Knitting instructions: fold over at the narrow bit to produce a kind of jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper with a high folded collar around the throat is named for that folded top.

clue.text: Maid's role is to serve rum, beer, stout …

indicators.note: rum in the sense of odd or strange tells us to rearrange the drink names that follow

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barmaid's job is pouring spirits, ale and porter for the customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like a third drink in the list, but it is the anagram signal: BEERSTOUT rearranged. 'is to serve' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: In comic opera a pert lady's servant is a stock part, so the name for that character type is a maid's role.

clue.text: Drive out in open carriage, waving one goodbye

indicators.note: waving goodbye, split around the word one, says that word leaves the carriage
goodbye joins waving to say the numeral departs from the carriage

parts.note: a chaise is a light open horse-drawn carriage
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a drive in a pony trap, waving farewell to a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving ... goodbye' sits either side of 'one', so I leaves CHAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel or send someone packing is to drive them away.

clue.text: Old-fashioned recipe used in set-piece restaurant set up

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
used in says the letters are found within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traditional dish features on the menu at a formal set-menu eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'used' in the definition, leaving the hidden word with no signal; 'used in' is that signal, and 'set up' turns TPIECER round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English the word for a written instruction for cooking a dish was the same as the one for a proof of payment.

clue.text: Appear to cause embarrassment

definitions.meaning: to arrive or turn up somewhere
to humiliate someone by outshining them or exposing them

explanation.surface: Turning up can make someone feel awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving is turning up, and exposing someone's faults so they look foolish is the other sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Capital ship is star attraction

parts.note: the capital of a column is its head or top
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A city's grand vessel is the main draw for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city, but here it is the top of a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: The performer billed at the top, the main act, is the star draw.

clue.text: Liquid central to bathhouse?

parts.note: the fluid without which a bathing establishment could not function

explanation.surface: Asking what fluid lies at the heart of a public bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Any bath or bathhouse depends on the commonest fluid of all for its whole purpose.

clue.text: Excuse fellow who's not himself?

annotationWithheld.why: Excuse fellow who's not himself? (6): PARDON is defined by Excuse, but no parse found for 'fellow who's not himself' giving PARDON letters

clue.text: Turning over, skip a page here and there in book

indicators.note: turning over says the whole run of pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: to skip is to miss out

explanation.surface: Flicking through, someone misses the odd page of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning over' reverses MISS + A + P as a whole, giving the Latin term.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word is used in references to mean that something occurs throughout a text, at scattered points.

clue.text: Girl left by air

parts.note: an aura is an air or atmosphere about someone

explanation.surface: A young woman departed by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by air' looks like travel; 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Original letter

definitions.meaning: as a noun, an eccentric or odd person
a written symbol of an alphabet

explanation.surface: Describing an authentic piece of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric individual is called a real one, and a printed symbol such as A or B is also this word.

clue.text: Places for kids to race about with trains

indicators.note: about says the word for race is turned back to front

parts.note: to race is to run
trains are sequences or series of things

explanation.surface: Playrooms where children dash around with toy railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' suggests toy railways, but here it means successions, as in a train of thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms or establishments where young children are looked after are places for small kids.

clue.text: Piece of music in major key

definitions.meaning: a slow movement, such as Handel's famous one
Key ..., the largest of the Florida Keys islands

explanation.surface: A composition written in a major tonality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks musical, but the second sense is an island: Key Largo is the biggest of the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow, broad movement takes its name from the Italian tempo mark, and the major Florida island shares it.

clue.text: Found in a pet, child is to be scolded

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
a chit is a young child, especially a girl

explanation.surface: A youngster found with the cat is going to be told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' reads like a container signal but is only link here, as is 'is'; a chit is an old word for a young girl or child.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to get into trouble and be told off.

clue.text: As dummies are, easily

definitions.meaning: in bridge the dummy's cards are laid out on the table
without effort, as in winning comfortably

explanation.surface: Shop mannequins are positioned with no difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, dummy is the partner whose cards are laid out for the declarer to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning with no effort is the idiom, and a bridge dummy's cards lie flat on the table.

clue.text: Press hack

definitions.meaning: a wringer that squeezes water from laundry

explanation.surface: Newspapers and their journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests journalism, but one sense is an old laundry roller and the other means to butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The roller device that squeezes wet washing, and as a verb to mutilate or ruin something.

clue.text: View that is seen during touchdown and take-off, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak says the combined words are pronounced to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: a touchdown is a landing, and a take-off can be an escape

explanation.surface: A scene glimpsed from an aircraft window as it lands and departs.
explanation.walkthrough: LAND plus ESCAPE, said quickly, sounds like the word for scenery. 'that is seen during' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad stretch of countryside seen at once is a scenic view.

clue.text: Worked a double shift? That's about right

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for right
shift says the letters of the words before it are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone who toiled through two consecutive shifts feels it is about fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work period, but it is the anagram signal for A DOUBLE, giving LABOUED, which goes 'about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil hard or strive is to work, in the past tense here.

clue.text: The interior of Brazil, say

parts.note: Brazil read as the nut, whose inside is the edible seed

explanation.surface: Talking about the inland regions of the South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: Brazil wants to be the country; it is the nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible inner seed of a nut is its core part.

clue.text: Mentioned saddle, referring to part of back

indicators.note: mentioned says the synonym for saddle is spoken, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: to saddle someone with a burden is to lumber them with it

explanation.surface: A rider talks about a saddle causing pain in the lower back.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the lower region of the spine, so it relates to part of the back.

clue.text: Eurasian shrub no good in African country

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation goes inside the country's name

parts.note: Syria is the country meant, though it lies in Asia

explanation.surface: A Eurasian bush fails to thrive in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Syria is in Asia, not Africa: the clue's 'African' is a slip, perhaps for 'Asian' or 'Arab'. NG goes 'in' SYRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The mock orange or lilac genus is a group of flowering bushes native to Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Crime witness reportedly unaffected

indicators.note: reportedly says the two words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a crime is a sin, and a witness is a seer, one who sees

explanation.surface: A criminal witness's account is said to be genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and free of pretence means without affectation.

clue.text: Very quietly slipping into user's disorderly quarters for drugs

indicators.note: slipping into says the musical letters go inside the jumbled word
disorderly says the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
pp, pianissimo, is the musical instruction for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoes into an addict's messy rooms looking for narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: pp is the musical mark pianissimo; 'quarters' only dresses the surface as the user's rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimulant pills such as amphetamines are slang-named for lifting the mood.

clue.text: Extract from collected papers

definitions.meaning: to squeeze out juice or oil
newspapers and journalists as a body

explanation.surface: Taking a passage from an anthology of documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezing to obtain juice is the verb, and newspapers together are the nation's journalism.

clue.text: Form of communication between the sexes, so to speak?

definitions.text: Form of communication between the sexes, so to speak?

parts.words: Form of communication between the sexes, so to speak?
parts.note: taken as a pun: female and male, spoken, suggest an electronic message

explanation.surface: Asking about how men and women talk to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'female' sounds like the electronic message.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic message sent over the internet is a means of communicating.

clue.text: Aims often set out in this?

definitions.text: Aims often set out in this?

indicators.note: set out says the letters of the preceding words are laid out afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party's goals are frequently listed in its policy document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges AIMS OFTEN; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A public declaration of a party's policies and goals is where aims are laid out.

clue.text: Coped with most of the leading characters

annotationWithheld.why: Coped with most of the leading characters (5): FACED is defined by Coped with, but the wordplay (five of the alphabet's first six letters, A to F, not in order) has no expression in the grammar
annotationWithheld.clue: Coped with most of the leading characters

clue.text: Making woman, babbling about nothing, dry up

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name

indicators.note: about says the word for babbling surrounds the zero

parts.note: to prate is to babble
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A chatterbox talks on about nothing until she runs dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' is link. PRATE goes 'about' O.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that disappears into vapour dries up, and figuratively a supply that vanishes does too.

clue.text: Seat Conservative got by a whisker

parts.note: a whisker is a single hair

explanation.surface: A Tory candidate won the constituency by the narrowest margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' and 'by a whisker' suggest an election; 'got by a' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of furniture for sitting on is a seat.

clue.text: Behind one's back, made advances to mum

indicators.note: behind places the word for made advances after the reversed letters
back says those letters are read in reverse

parts.note: one is I, and one's is I plus S
to lend money is to make an advance, so made advances means lent

explanation.surface: Someone secretly made passes at a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' wants to be a mother; it means saying nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to stay quiet, so mum here is the adjective for saying nothing.

clue.text: Unenterprising type employed to tidy up plant

definitions.meaning: a dull, idle or useless person
to remove spent flowers from a plant

explanation.surface: A lazy worker is hired to do the gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull, idle person is slang-named this, and snipping off faded blooms from a plant is the gardening verb.
